A cool little budget mini shooter with some puzzle elements. There is a logical progression that's simple but fun to figure out, as you are progressing through each stage while collecting crystals and powerups to buy and upgrade ships. The only distinguishing factor between this and a bajillion other games is the "puzzle" element. Basically, when you shoot an alien the outside aliens freeze and basically become immovable blocks you must navigate around. Obviously, you want to target bigger block clusters because this will create more clear open spaces. 

It gets harder as you progress because the game introduces other obstacles like mines, spikes, flying enemies, etc. The boss fights are drastically different, as these are more skill-based with fast moving projectiles. Your weapon even auto shoots bullets whereas previously you had to calculate single shots to make sure you don't get trapped. There are only six stages. The collectibles took me about fifteen minutes and then there is a "Boss rush" mode that's a joke and can be completed in a couple minutes if you know what to do. I went ahead and did bosh rush mode on "hard" just for the heck of it and the only difference the projectiles move faster, but they go down so easy it doesn't even matter.

This game has beautiful graphics and would be a gem if it was a little longer and more in-depth, but even for a forgettable one-time experience it's fine.

🧩 puzzle de cores

Very cute little retro pixel art style game perfect for the Steam Deck. There are 6 stages total and they are split up between puzzle section and boss section. During the puzzle section, you have to blast aliens to clear a path. The boss sections play out as your typical bullet hell shooter and can be quite the challenge. You should get a good few hours of fun out of this cute little game.

Worth noting however, if you plan on getting all achievements, they seem to only be properly tracked and unlocked on Windows. I beat the game and did everything including boss rush on the Steam Deck, but nothing unlocked. So, I installed it on my Windows desktop, then used steam input to configure turbo mode on the shoot button. This helped me beat the whole game again and get all achievements in less than an hour.

So I fundamentally LIKE THIS GAME.  It's a good genre hybrid between falling block and shmups.  The art is good, the game engine is good, the core gameplay works.

However, the progression system is fundamentally a PIECE OF TRASH.  The progression system should NOT have been included.  When in doubt, your shmup should have as much progression as the old-school arcade games:  Zero.  None.  Nada,

1) [b]There aren't enough upgrades to max out every ship in the game.[/b]  Progression-based games create completionists (I am one of these), and a game where you can't do [i]everything[/i] is a frustrating non-starter.  When you included a progression system in your game, you inherently promised me that I could 'get' everything in your game.  Nope.

SOLUTION:  Let me spend gems on upgrades?  Let me play new-game plus to get more upgrade items?  idk

2) [b]Choosing the right ship for each stage is not an interesting choice.[/b]  You're basically making us pass a weird knowledge check.  There's usually a "correct" choice for each stage, where you're choosing a ship that can resist the stage hazards.  This isn't a gameplay choice, this is a basic knowledge check.  (When combined with the limited upgrades, you're also playing with ships that you haven't upgraded and will never upgrade...)

SOLUTION:  Include only one ship in the game, and remove enemies from your game completely.  If you don't want me to play around your enemies, just don't include them!

3) [b]What power level am I supposed to be?[/b]  This is fundamentally my problem with progression-based systems.  You're rewarding skilled players by,,, making the game easier.  How many hits do you expect me to have for each stage?  How many shots should it take to defeat each enemy?  How fast should my ship move?  There are no correct answers to any of these questions, because it changes over the course of the game.

The beginning of the game is a frustrating grind because it takes [i]six shots[/i] to destroy a jellyfish.  Why does it take that many shots?  To make you feel relief at the end of the game when you can kill them with one shot.  This kind of design is not okay.

SOLUTION:  No upgrades!  Your ship should start the game at its final power level.  Pick a power level, and balance your game around that.


If you want ambiguity and replay value in your game, just give me a scoring system.  You can even make survival easy and scoring a challenge; this is what Astebreed does.

(Casual onlookers might rightly point out that most traditional horizontal shmups feature powerups and ask, why omit them if the classics did?  To which I would answer, later titles like Giga Wing and Progear both reduced powerups to a formality, and this was a good design change.  You can max out your power in the first stage of these games, and then you stay at full power for the rest of the game.  You technically have to recover after a death and scoop your powerups back up after you drop them, but this powerup design makes collection an aesthetic process and not truly integral to the design.  Power-ups are honestly just a tool to suck in genre newbies at the arcade and make them think that they're playing well, even if they're not.)

The dev encouraged players who completed the game to leave a review, so I will! :3

This was a nice little game. A mix between shmup and color matching to proceed, with a small collect-a-thon in collecting the emeralds and ship upgrades from the distinctly but only-so-slightly different-looking aliens you have to destroy to get them, and bullet hell boss challenges at every stage's end that might greatly challenge those who aren't too familiar with the shmup genre.

I think one thing that really doesn't get enough love in video game reviews anymore these days, is sound design. I liked the player ship pilot's little quips during the stages per situational circumstance, and boy-oh-boy, this has to be said: The music here is AMAZING! It's like someone here who developed this game is WELL-schooled in what makes GOOD retro-stylized video game music, and it shows. The title screen theme, the "Jungle Planet" theme, and the "Barren Planet" theme, are three themes that particularly stand out. I loved the rest as well. Not enough games have "jingles" for when you triumph or lose, a la classic Metal Gear Solid. Big ups to these devs for showing every aspiring chip and retro-stylized musician how it's done! 👍

How MUCH would I recommend this game to others? (Since Steam recommendations are a flat yes or no). That depends on how much you love simplistic, classic-style shmups. It has a very basic "upgrade system." Just collect three types of upgrades: Health, Attack, and Speed, and apply them to unlockable ships, which all have specific specialties in what they defend against. Make your way through large walls of aliens in auto-scrolling stages without restricting your own progress. Simple "Lose and start over" flow, but the stages are very, very short. It's a hyper-challenging yet casual ride that lasts a short while or longer depending on your skill level and intuition. I'm usually hesitant to give games I really like less than a solid rating of 10 (No game is perfect), but suffice to say, pick this one up if you're in the market for a miniature set of "puzzle shmup" challenges. It's no "Star of Providence" (formerly called "Monolith: Relics of the Past"), but grab it on sale. Full price if you want to support the devs.

シューティングゲームにパズル要素が加わった新感覚パズルシューティング。
ゲームの流れとしてはパズル要素のあるステージ道中を抜けて、ラストでステージボスとガチシューティングバトルという感じ。パズル要素ありだが操作感は一貫してシューティングのそれで統一されている。

ステージは全６面。各ステージ道中にはエイリアンがひしめき合っており撃破しながら進むのだが、撃破したエイリアンの四方にいたエイリアンは結晶化してしまう。こうなってしまうとどうやっても突破できなくなってしまうので、移動範囲内の前方が全てそれで塞がれてしまうとゲームオーバーを待つのみとなる。
エイリアンは色分けされており同色のエイリアンが隣接している場合は連鎖が可能。任意の１体を撃破すると繋がっている同色のエイリアンたちは連鎖爆発していき上記の結晶化は連鎖の終端で起こる。
以上のことからステージ道中はいかに連鎖を狙って進路を確保するか、ということになる。
また各ステージには「グリーンエメラルド」と「アップグレードポイント」を持った特殊エイリアンがそれぞれ３体存在し撃破すると入手できる。
「グリーンエメラルド」はストーリーアイテム的なものでゲーム的に使い道があるわけではないが「アップグレードポイント」は消費することで機体の対応する能力を強化できる。全機体フル強化するには数が足りないので考えて使おう。

通常のエイリアンは触れてもダメージはないのでパズルに集中できるが各ステージ毎に固有の攻撃性を持ったエイリアンやギミックが存在し攻略を難しくしている。
エイリアンを撃破することでジェムを入手でき、そのジェムによって能力の違う自機をアンロックできる。自機によっては攻撃性エイリアンやギミックを無効化する能力を持っているので、そういった能力を優先するか攻防力の高い機体を選ぶか選択の幅がある。
ジェムは繰り返し遊んでると余ってくるが全機体をアンロックした後は特に使い道が無い。「アップグレードポイント」を購入でもできればよかったのだが。

各ステージラストはボスとのシューティングバトル。ボスの攻撃は一定時間ごとに切り替わり数種類のパターンから毎回ランダムで選ばれる。
シューティングとしての難易度はやや易しめといったところ。基本的に見てから避けられるパターンの攻撃がほとんどなのでシューティング上級者には物足りないかもしれないが、個人的には適度な歯ごたえで良い。
全ステージクリア後は実績にも絡むボスラッシュで遊べるが各ステージ攻略では使いづらかったボス戦特化の機体が満を持して活躍できるのでこちらも苦戦はしないだろう。

ゲームとしてのボリュームは比較的コンパクトだがキチンとまとまった良いゲーム。
パズル要素もシューティング要素も難しすぎず簡単すぎず良バランスで楽しく遊べた。おすすめ。

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

[h1]Um bom jogo de nave![/h1]

Apenas esse título resume muito bem este jogo. Em todas as camadas do que esse game se dispõe a fazer, ele cumpre com méritos. A trilha sonora é muito gostosa e combina bem com a vibe do projeto, o [i]voice actor[/i] do piloto é sensacional e a [i]cutscene[/i] inicial apresentando o conceito do game me fez sentir jogando um jogo de [b]SNES[/b].

A arte é muito simples (é só o que se espera de um jogo clássico de navinha). Minha única alfinetada talvez fique exatamente aqui. Algumas escolhas de design podem causar confusão enquanto jogamos. Os "mundos" ao qual jogamos não estão dispostos no mapa de forma linear, então as vezes você vai entrar no mundo 3 achando que é o mundo 2, por exemplo. Isso não é necessariamente um problema, porém um jogador menos habituado com esse tipo de jogo pode se frustrar ao ir em uma fase mais difícil sem ter a nave correta para tal. Alguns dos aliens que dropam atualizações para nave também são muito parecidos com aliens comuns, o que fez eu esquecê-los pelo mapa várias vezes.

Fora isso, o game não tem nada que cause uma inconveniência ou raiva gigante. O nível de dificuldade é justo e você ganha a quantidade perfeita de pontos para atualizar sua nave ou comprar novas quando for preciso, não tive que grindar pontos para naves em momento algum durante o jogo.

É uma pena que seja tão curto, porém se não fosse talvez perdesse sua graça!

I am not a shmup player, but the puzzle aspect of Super Star Path attracted me. Unfortunately, the puzzle aspect is either poorly thought out or intended to titillate shmup fans.

Basically, shot placement and position are more important than in any other shmup I've ever played. Each level, you'll be up against rows of enemies, only some of which will shoot back. Any enemy that you manage to shoot by itself or in groups of same/matching type will produce a gem for you to collect. However, enemies killed in mixed groups will cause other enemies in the group to freeze. Frozen enemies cannot be destroyed. Add in obstacles that cannot be destroyed, obstacles that are difficult to destroy, and enemies that shoot back, and suddenly you're both creating your own maze in real time and trying to remain aware of the threats surrounding you.

I tried the "Easy" mode, and I can say with confidence at this point that Super Star Path is a game for shmup enthusiasts only!

Nice looking and sounding minimalist game, but every design decision at best conflicts with another, and at worst is so at odds with the game's genre that it's unclear what the goal was. Take a shooter with a selection of classes, stats you can upgrade, and selectable levels with unique challenges. Now make the classes locked behind beating the levels, make the upgrade materials finite and non-refundable, and levels with unclear obstacles until you play through them.

Next, is the game a puzzle game, or a top down shoot em up? The answer is both, as long as bad versions of things count. There is no puzzle as much as there is a single rule that punishes you for failing to deal with the obstacles in the "right" way. Right wouldn't be written in quotes if the game's levels weren't entirely random, and if the player didn't lack any tools for manipulating the random field to turn bad layouts into good layouts. Think playing Tetris, except you can't flip the blocks and you have this game's design. It's also not a good shoot em up because the things that attack back work on different rules than the puzzle blocks. They only die when you shoot them a bunch, but they're very easily and very often hidden behind invincible blocks that prevent you from destroying them. The game also quickly restricts your movement, not with difficult bullet patterns, but with walls, taking the enjoyment of dodging those patterns away until you get to a simple boss at the end with 2-3 patterns.

TL;DR, you lack the tools and deliberate stage design required for a good puzzle, and you lack the skill-based shoot and dodge progression required for a shmup. What you're left with is a game where mashing the shoot button while you move left and right wins a the "stage" as often as skill or thought, and with bosses too uninteresting to compare to any other shmup game on Steam. Buy only if it's on sale for a buck and you just want something to give you some achievements for minimal effort.

Another banger by DYA Games, and one that's been on my radar for a while as a shmup fan. DYA's games are concentrated, faithful and fresh-this older title of theirs holds up to that too!

The game takes a Mega-Man style approach to level selection, which serves the game well since every planet has its own challenges. Levels are short and dense, and even though it takes a minute to get familiar with the puzzle solving, it gets really fun to figure out good pathing and get through the swarms more and more efficiently. Aside from the occasional wonky diagonal hitbox, the gameplay is incredibly solid. A short boss at the end is a nice final burst of intensity for each level- And bloody hard, at that. People more interested in the puzzle aspect than the combat may be introduced to one heck of a difficulty curve.

There's plenty of ships to choose from, and pickups within the levels to upgrade them- Some offering resistances/answers to specific obstacles, or the most interesting of which granting a new shot pattern for use in the boss fight- I would have liked to see more ships designed like this! Unlocking ships isn't too expensive either, no unnecessary frustration from this system. Maybe it wouldn't have hurt to be able to max out any ship, and maybe gems could have been handy for paying for upgrades- i found my gems racking up and stopped being useful quickly when I was stuck on a level.

There's [spoiler]a Boss Rush mode available as[/spoiler] one last challenge to those who want to keep going, but the bulk of the game is just trying to clear the main story. Really, it's just a short and sweet game with a clear vision and plenty of thought put into it. If the action looks endearing by the looks of the trailer, you will get what you pay for! Consider Strikey Sisters and Bot Vice if you'd like a longer arcade experience made by these developers!
